photo_findings.shows: An oblique left-side exterior view of a Ford tractor chassis among closely parked trucks.
strengths: The visible steer tire has substantial tread above the wear indicators, with no obvious shoulder collapse, sidewall bulge or cracking.
The visible drive tires retain pronounced tread blocks and show no visible sidewall damage.
The visible chassis rail is straight, with paint attached and no lifting scale, perforation or repair plate apparent.
The fuel-tank casing appears complete and undistorted; visible dullness is consistent with road film and service wear.
The visible rear lamp cluster is complete, with unbroken lenses and a straight carrier.
The visible rear mudguard is present, straight and free of obvious cracks.
The visible drive tires carry matching tread patterns, with tread standing well proud of the wear bars and no evident irregular shoulder wear or sidewall damage.
The visible drive tires retain clearly defined tread grooves with no obvious cupping or abnormal shoulder wear.
cannot_tell: The fifth-wheel plate, jaw throat and mounting hardware are not visible; an elevated rear-quarter photograph is required.
The catwalk and suzie coils are obscured by the cab and overlapping chassis.
Rear lamp clusters, wiring, mudflaps and their brackets cannot be assigned reliably because adjacent trucks overlap this vehicle.
Drive-tire brand matching and wear across the complete axle require square rear and opposite-side photographs.
Crossmember ends, air bags, shocks and air-line condition need clear close rear-underbody photographs.
Mechanical condition, fluid leakage and coupling operation cannot be determined from this exterior view.

strengths: Visible front cab panels and bumper sit square, with parallel gaps and no evident distortion.

photo_findings.shows: Close-up of a drive-axle dual-tire assembly with part of the rim and chassis visible.

issues.observation: The outer dual has a broad shoulder scrub band worn noticeably below the centre ribs, with local chunking along the tread edge; this is uneven wear beyond the stated distance and calls for tire replacement plus pressure, alignment and suspension checks. The angle does not prove that the lowest area is level with the wear bars or expose casing, either of which would require immediate removal from service.
issues.severity_reason: The local shoulder scrub merits measurement and geometry checks, but one uncorroborated view against otherwise sound drive-tire views does not establish end-of-life condition or a replacement job.

issues.observation: The outer drive tire has a broad, near-smooth outer shoulder with circumferential chunking, while the paired inner tire retains substantially deeper tread; replacement should be booked and inflation, dual matching and axle alignment checked, with immediate withdrawal required if an on-truck gauge confirms the shoulder at or below the wear bars.

The outer drive tire has widespread irregular block wear and chunking, with the outer shoulder visibly lower than the centre rows; it is at replacement-planning condition and warrants inflation, alignment and suspension checks. The wear appears heavier than expected for the stated distance, although the wear bars are not clear enough here to establish illegal tread depth.

strengths: The inner dual's visible crown retains defined tread blocks and grooves standing proud of the wear bars.
No bulge, exposed cord or casing-deep cut is visible on the exposed outer sidewall.
The visible rim edge appears straight, without an evident crack or heavy kerbing.
The inner drive tire's visible tread remains clearly proud of the wear bars, without obvious cupping or scalloping.
The visible rim edge appears straight and free of cracking.
cannot_tell: A tread gauge and square-on view of the wear bars are needed to establish remaining depth and current legal status at the worn shoulder.
The opposite-side drive tires are not shown, so axle-wide brand, pattern and wear matching cannot be confirmed.
DOT date codes and any retread buff line or cap edge are not legible.
Wheel nuts and indicators, valve stem, hub and brake area are obscured.
A perpendicular tread-gauge photograph is needed to confirm remaining depth and road legality at the outer tire's worn shoulder.
Exact tread depth relative to every wear bar requires a gauge reading and closer square-on tread photographs.

adjustment.basis: capped at one residual standard deviation of the price model (+/-9.4%) - the variation in asking price that year, kilometres, brand and market do not explain
adjustment.cap_basis: measured: one out-of-fold residual standard deviation of the price model (+/-9.4%) - the variation in asking price that year, kilometres, brand and market do not explain
adjustment.weights_basis: assumed, not fitted: the severity x impact weight table, the per-subsystem saturation decay, the family value weights and the coverage thresholds are all hand-set. This corpus carries no condition ground truth to fit them against, so they are stated rather than measured
notes: 34% of the truck was affirmed sound, but the comparable band is what an AVERAGE-condition truck is asked for, and only a truck this system will call excellent is priced above it

asking.label: in line with the market
asking.summary: The asking price sits inside the band that comparable trucks of this age and mileage are listed at.

widened: only 74% of the truck by value was photographed legibly, so the condition band widens 1.09x (an assumption, not a measurement)
the synthesis pass graded this fair and the deterministic rollup grades it good, so the condition band widens 1.08x (an assumption)
caveats: Trained on ASKING prices, not realised sale prices - the honest caveat, not a hidden one. Expect realised prices to sit below the band.

The measured interval coverage belongs to the comparable-asking band. The condition-adjusted band is that estimate moved by what the photos show, which is a deliberate departure from what sellers ask and is not covered by the same measurement.
Turkish prices converted at 48.596 TRY/USD as of 2026-09-11; at ~30% annual inflation this rate goes stale fast - refit rather than quote it later.
The Turkish comparables are brand-concentrated (78 of 84 Turkish listings are FORD), so an unfamiliar make is priced off the market average rather than off its own curve.
